nodes.name: Characterization of Horn theories in predicate fuzzy logics
nodes.statement: Cintula and H\'ajek raised the open question of characterizing theories of Horn clauses in predicate fuzzy logics \cite{CiHa10}.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
also_stated_at: Our next objective is to solve the open problem of characterizing theories of Horn clauses in predicate fuzzy logics, formulated by Cintula and H\'ajek in \cite{CiHa10}.
nodes.statement_short: Characterize theories of Horn clauses in predicate fuzzy logics.

nodes.name: MTL-algebra
nodes.statement: The logic MTL$\forall^m$ is the predicate extension of the left-continuous t-norm based logic MTL introduced in \cite{EsGo01}, where MTL-algebras are defined as bounded integral commutative residuated lattices $(A,\sqcap,\sqcup,*,\Rightarrow,0,1)$, where $\sqcap$ and $\sqcup$ are respectively the lattice meet and join operations and $(\Rightarrow,*)$ is a residuated pair, satisfying the pre-linearity equation $(x\Rightarrow y)\sqcup(y\Rightarrow x)=1$ (for an exhaustive exposition of MTL-algebras, see \cite{NoEsGis05}).
nodes.section: 2 Preliminaires
differentia: satisfying the pre-linearity equation $(x\Rightarrow y)\sqcup(y\Rightarrow x)=1$
nodes.statement_short: MTL$\forall^m$ extends MTL; MTL-algebras are prelinear bounded integral commutative residuated lattices.

nodes.name: Completeness of MTL / Jenei-Montagna standard completeness
nodes.statement: In addition, completeness of this logic with respect to MTL-algebras is proven in \cite[Th.1]{EsGo01}, and Jenei and Montagna shown that MTL is the logic of all left continuous t-norms and their residua \cite{JeMon02}.
nodes.section: 2 Preliminaires
conclusions: completeness of this logic with respect to MTL-algebras
MTL is the logic of all left continuous t-norms and their residua
nodes.statement_short: MTL is complete w.r.t. MTL-algebras and is the logic of left-continuous t-norms.

nodes.name: Predicate language
nodes.statement: A \emph{predicate language} $\mathcal{P}$ is a triple $\left\langle Pred_{\mathcal{P}},Func_{\mathcal{P}},Ar_{\mathcal{P}} \right\rangle$, where $Pred_{\mathcal{P}}$ is a nonempty set of \emph{predicate symbols}, $Func_{\mathcal{P}}$ is a set of \emph{function symbols} (disjoint from $Pred_{\mathcal{P}}$), and $Ar_{\mathcal{P}}$ represents the \emph{arity function}, which assigns a natural number to each predicate symbol or function symbol. We call this natural number the \emph{arity of the symbol}. The predicate symbols with arity zero are called \emph{truth constants}, while the function symbols whose arity is zero are named \emph{individual constants} (\emph{constants} for short) or \emph{objects}.
nodes.section: 2 Preliminaires
nodes.statement_short: A predicate language is a triple of predicate symbols, function symbols and an arity function; zero-arity symbols are truth constants / individual constants.

nodes.name: Ground term
nodes.statement: A term $t$ is \emph{ground} if it has no variables.
nodes.section: 2 Preliminaires

nodes.name: Equality as a non-logical predicate
nodes.statement: Throughout the paper we consider the equality symbol as a binary predicate symbol, not as a logical symbol, that is, the equality symbol is not necessarily present in all the languages and its interpretation is not fixed.
nodes.section: 2 Preliminaires

nodes.name: Core fuzzy logic $L$
nodes.statement: From now on, let $L$ be a core fuzzy logic in a propositional language $\mathcal{L}$ that contains only the truth-constants $\overline{1}$ and $\overline{0}$ (for an extended study of core fuzzy logics, see \cite{CiHa10}).
nodes.section: 2 Preliminaires

nodes.name: Axiomatic system of $L\forall^m$
nodes.statement: We introduce an axiomatic system for the predicate logic $L\forall^m$: \begin{description} \item[($\mathrm{P}$)]$\space\space$ $\space\space$ $\space\space$ Instances of the axioms of $L$ (the propositional variables are substituted for first-order formulas). \item[($\forall 1$)]$\space\space$ $(\forall x)\varphi(x)\rightarrow\varphi(t)$, where the term $t$ is substitutable for $x$ in $\varphi$. \item[($\exists1$)]$\space\space$ $\varphi(t)\rightarrow(\exists x)\varphi(x)$, where the term $t$ is substitutable for $x$ in $\varphi$. \item[($\forall 2$)]$\space\space$ $(\forall x)(\xi\rightarrow\varphi)\rightarrow(\xi\rightarrow(\forall x)\varphi(x))$, where $x$ is not free in $\xi$. \item[($\exists2$)]$\space\space$ $(\forall x)(\varphi\rightarrow\xi)\rightarrow((\exists x)\varphi\rightarrow\xi)$, where $x$ is not free in $\xi$. \end{description} The deduction rules of $L\forall^m$ are those of $L$ and the rule of generalization: from $\varphi$ infer $(\forall x)\varphi$. The definitions of proof and provability are analogous to the classical ones. We denote by $\Phi\vdash_{L\forall^m}\varphi$ the fact that $\varphi$ is provable in $L\forall^m$ from the set of formulas $\Phi$. For the sake of clarity, when it is clear from the context we will write $\vdash$ to refer to $\vdash_{L\forall^m}$. A set of formulas $\Phi$ is \emph{consistent} if $\Phi\not\vdash\overline{0}$.
nodes.section: 2 Preliminaires
nodes.statement_short: Hilbert-style axioms (P), (forall1), (exists1), (forall2), (exists2) plus generalization define $L\forall^m$, provability $\vdash$ and consistency.

nodes.name: Semantics of Predicate Fuzzy Logics
nodes.statement: Consider a predicate language $\mathcal{P}=\langle Pred_{\mathcal{P}}, Func_{\mathcal{P}}, Ar_{\mathcal{P}} \rangle$ and let \textbf{A} be an $L$-algebra. We define an $\textbf{A}$\emph{-structure} $\mathrm{\mathbf{M}}$ for $\mathcal{P}$ as the triple $\langle M, (P_M)_{P\in Pred}, (F_M)_{F\in Func} \rangle$, where $M$ is a nonempty domain, $P_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}}}$ is an $n$-ary fuzzy relation for each $n$-ary predicate symbol, i.e., a function from $M^n$ to $\textbf{A}$, identified with an element of $\textbf{A}$ if $n=0$; and $F_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}}}$ is a function from $M^n$ to $M$, identified with an element of $M$ if $n=0$. As usual, if $\mathrm{\mathbf{M}}$ is an $\textbf{A}$-structure for $\mathcal{P}$, an $\mathrm{\mathbf{M}}$-evaluation of the object variables is a mapping $v$ assigning to each object variable an element of $M$. The set of all object variables is denoted by $Var$. If $v$ is an $\mathrm{\mathbf{M}}$-evaluation, $x$ is an object variable and $a\in M$, we denote by $v[x\mapsto a]$ the $\mathrm{\mathbf{M}}$-evaluation so that $v[x\mapsto a](x)=a$ and $v[x\mapsto a](y)=v(y)$ for $y$ an object variable such that $y\not=x$. If $\mathrm{\mathbf{M}}$ is an $\textbf{A}$-structure and $v$ is an $\mathrm{\mathbf{M}}$-evaluation, we define the \emph{values} of terms and the \emph{truth values} of formulas in $M$ for an evaluation $v$ recursively as follows: \begin{description} \item $||x||^{\small{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v}=v(x)$; \item $||F(t_1,\ldots,t_n)||^{\small{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v}=F_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}}}(||t_1||^{\small{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v},\ldots,||t_n||^{\small{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v})$, for $F\in Func$; \item $||P(t_1,\ldots,t_n)||^{\small{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v}=P_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}}}(||t_1||^{\small{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v},\ldots,||t_n||^{\small{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v})$, for $P\in Pred$; \item $||c(\varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_n)||^{\small{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v}=c_{\textbf{A}}(||\varphi_1||^{\small{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v},\ldots,||\varphi_n||^{\small{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v})$, for $c\in\mathcal{L}$; \item $||(\forall x)\varphi||^{\small{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v}=inf\{||\varphi||^{\small{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v[x\rightarrow a]}\mid a\in M\}$; \item $||(\exists x)\varphi||^{\small{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v}=sup\{||\varphi||^{\small{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v[x\rightarrow a]}\mid a\in M\}$. \end{description} If the infimum or the supremum do not exist, we take the truth value of the formula as undefined. We say that an $\textbf{A}$-structure is \emph{safe} if $||\varphi||^{\small{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v}$ is defined for each formula $\varphi$ and each $\mathrm{\mathbf{M}}$-evaluation $v$.
nodes.section: 2 Preliminaires
nodes.statement_short: A-structures interpret predicates as A-valued relations; Tarskian truth values via inf/sup for quantifiers; safe = all values defined.
nodes.label: evaluation

nodes.name: $||\Phi||=1$ for a set of formulas
nodes.statement: For a set of formulas $\Phi$, we write $||\Phi||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v}=1$ if $||\varphi||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v}=1$ for every $\varphi\in\Phi$.
nodes.section: 2 Preliminaires

nodes.name: Model of a set of formulas
nodes.statement: We say that $\langle\emph{\textbf{A}},\mathrm{\mathbf{M}}\rangle$ is a \emph{model of a set of formulas $\Phi$} if $||\varphi ||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v}=1$ for any $\varphi\in\Phi$ and any \textbf{M}-evaluation $v$.
nodes.section: 2 Preliminaires
nodes.definiendum: model of a set of formulas $\Phi$

nodes.name: $||\varphi||_{\mathbf{M}}=1$
nodes.statement: We denote by $||\varphi||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\textbf{M}}=1$ that $||\varphi||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\textbf{M},v}=1$ for all \textbf{M}-evaluation $v$.
nodes.section: 2 Preliminaires

nodes.name: Satisfiable formula
nodes.statement: We say that a formula $\varphi$ is \emph{satisfiable} if there exists a structure $\langle\emph{\textbf{{A}}},\textbf{M}\rangle$ such that $||\varphi||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\textbf{M}}=1$.
nodes.section: 2 Preliminaires

nodes.name: Structure (convention)
nodes.statement: Unless otherwise stated, from now on \emph{\textbf{A}} denotes an MTL-algebra and we refer to \emph{\textbf{A}}-structures simply as \emph{structures}.
nodes.section: 2 Preliminaires

nodes.name: Homomorphism between fuzzy structures
nodes.statement: {\em \textbf{\cite[Definition 6]{DeGaNo14}}} $\space$ Let $\langle\textbf{A},\mathrm{\mathbf{M}}\rangle$ and $\langle\textbf{B},\mathrm{\mathbf{N}}\rangle$ be structures, $f$ be a mapping from $\textbf{A}$ to $\textbf{B}$ and $g$ be a mapping from $M$ to $N$. The pair $\langle f,g\rangle$ is said to be a \emph{homomorphism} from $\langle\textbf{A},\mathrm{\mathbf{M}}\rangle$ to $\langle\textbf{B},\mathrm{\mathbf{N}}\rangle$ if $f$ is a homomorphism of ${L}$-algebras and for every $n$-ary function symbol $F$ and $d_1,\ldots,d_n\in M$, $$g(F_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}}}(d_1,\ldots,d_n))=F_{\mathrm{\mathbf{N}}}(g(d_1),\ldots,g(d_n)) $$ \noindent and for every $n$-ary predicate symbol $P$ and $d_1,\ldots,d_n\in M$, $$ \text{ \emph{(*) }} \text{If }P_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}}}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)=1 \text{, then } P_{\mathrm{\mathbf{N}}}(g(d_1),\ldots,g(d_n))=1.$$ We say that a homomorphism $\langle f,g\rangle$ is \emph{strict} if instead of \emph{(*)} it satisfies the stronger condition: for every $n$-ary predicate symbol $P$ and $d_1,\ldots,d_n\in M$, $$P_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}}}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)=1 \text{ if and only if } P_{\mathrm{\mathbf{N}}}(g(d_1),\ldots,g(d_n))=1.$$ \noindent Moreover we say that $\langle f,g\rangle$ is an \emph{embedding} if it is a strict homomorphism and both functions $f$ and $g$ are injective. And we say that an embedding $\langle f,g\rangle$ is an \emph{isomorphism} if both functions $f$ and $g$ are surjective.
nodes.section: 2 Preliminaires
nodes.statement_short: A homomorphism is a pair (algebra homomorphism, domain map) preserving functions and truth-value-1 atomic facts; strict/embedding/isomorphism strengthen it.
nodes.label: def:mapping structures

nodes.name: Classical basic Horn formula
nodes.statement: In classical predicate logic, a \emph{basic Horn formula} is a formula of the form $ \alpha_{1}\wedge\dotsb \wedge\alpha_{n}\rightarrow\beta$, where $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n,\beta$ are atomic formulas.
nodes.section: 3 Horn clauses

nodes.name: Basic Horn Formula
nodes.statement: A \emph{basic Horn formula} is a formula of the form \begin{equation} \alpha_1\&\dotsb\&\alpha_n\rightarrow\beta \hfill \end{equation} where $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n, \beta$ are atomic formulas.
nodes.section: 3 Horn clauses
nodes.label: strong basic

nodes.name: Basic Horn formula shape
nodes.statement: \alpha_1\&\dotsb\&\alpha_n\rightarrow\beta \hfill
nodes.section: 3 Horn clauses

nodes.name: Basic weak Horn formula
nodes.statement: The formula obtained by substitution in expression (\ref{1}) of the strong conjunction $\&$ by the weak conjunction $\wedge$ will be called \emph{basic weak Horn formula}.
nodes.section: 3 Horn clauses

nodes.name: Basic w-Horn formula (notation)
nodes.statement: From now on, for the sake of clarity, we will refer to the basic weak Horn formulas as \emph{basic w-Horn formulas}.
nodes.section: 3 Horn clauses

nodes.name: Disjunctive Horn forms are not equivalent
nodes.statement: Analogously to classical logic, disjunctive definitions of basic Horn formulas can be defined. Nevertheless, it is an easy exercise to check that, for predicate fuzzy logics, these disjunctive forms are not in general equivalent to the implicational ones that we have introduced here.
nodes.section: 3 Horn clauses

nodes.name: Quantifier-free (w-)Horn formula
nodes.statement: A \emph{quantifier-free Horn formula} is a formula of the form \newline $\phi_1\&\dotsb\&\phi_m$ where $m\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\phi_i$ is a basic Horn formula for every $1\leq i\leq m$. If $\phi_i$ is a basic w-Horn formula for every $1\leq i\leq m$, we say that $\phi_1\wedge\dotsb\wedge\phi_m$ is a \emph{quantifier-free w-Horn formula}.
nodes.section: 3 Horn clauses
nodes.label: qf Horn

nodes.name: (w-) notation
nodes.statement: From now on, whenever it is possible, we present a unique definition for both the strong and the weak version, we use the \emph{w-} symbol into parenthesis.
nodes.section: 3 Horn clauses

nodes.name: (w-)Horn formula, (w-)Horn clause, universal Horn theory
nodes.statement: A \emph{(w-)Horn formula} is a formula of the form $Q\gamma$, where $Q$ is a (possibly empty) string of quantifiers $(\forall x),(\exists x)$... and $\gamma$ is a quantifier-free (w-)Horn formula. A \emph{(w-)Horn clause} (or \emph{universal (w-)Horn formula}) is a (w-)Horn formula in which the quantifier prefix (if any) has only universal quantifiers. A \emph{(w-)universal Horn theory} is a set of (w-)Horn clauses.
nodes.section: 3 Horn clauses
nodes.statement_short: Horn formulas are quantified quantifier-free Horn formulas; Horn clauses have only universal quantifiers; universal Horn theories are sets of them.
nodes.label: Horn

nodes.name: Recursive definition of classical Horn clauses
nodes.statement: Observe that, in classical logic, the formula $(\forall x)\varphi \wedge (\forall x) \psi$ is logically equivalent to $(\forall x)(\varphi \wedge \psi).$ This result can be used to prove that every Horn clause is equivalent in classical logic to a conjunction of formulas of the form $(\forall x_1) \ldots (\forall x_k)\varphi$, where $\varphi$ is a basic Horn formula. Having in mind these equivalences, it is easy to see that the set of all Horn clauses is recursively defined in classical logic by the following rules: \begin{itemize} \item[1.] If $\varphi$ is a basic Horn formula, then $\varphi$ is a Horn clause; \item[2.] If $\varphi$ and $\psi$ are Horn clauses, then $\varphi\wedge\psi$ is a Horn clause; \item[3.] If $\varphi$ is a Horn clause, then $(\forall x)\varphi$ is a Horn clause. \end{itemize}
nodes.section: 3 Horn clauses
nodes.statement_short: In classical logic Horn clauses are recursively generated from basic Horn formulas by conjunction and universal quantification.

nodes.name: Horn clauses are not recursively defined in MTL
nodes.statement: In MTL$\forall^m$ we can deduce $(\forall x)\varphi \wedge (\forall x) \psi\leftrightarrow(\forall x)(\varphi \wedge \psi)$. This fact allows us to show that in MTL$\forall^m$, any w-Horn clause is equivalent to a weak conjunction of formulas of the form $(\forall x_1)\dotsb(\forall x_k)(\varphi)$ where $\varphi$ is a basic w-Horn formula. Thus, w-Horn clauses can be recursively defined in MTL$\forall^m$ as above. But it is not the case for the strong conjunction since $(\forall x)\varphi \& (\forall x) \psi\leftrightarrow(\forall x)(\varphi \& \psi)$ can not be deduced from MTL$\forall^m$ (we refer to \cite[Remark p.281]{EsGo01}). So the set of Horn clauses is not recursively defined in MTL$\forall^m$.
nodes.section: 3 Horn clauses
nodes.statement_short: w-Horn clauses admit the classical recursive definition in MTL$\forall^m$, but strong-conjunction Horn clauses do not.

nodes.name: Similarity symbol
nodes.statement: From now on we assume that we work in a language with a binary predicate symbol $\approx$ interpreted as a similarity.

nodes.name: Similarity axioms in the logic
nodes.statement: We assume also that the axiomatization of the logic $L\forall^m$ contains the following axioms for $\approx$.
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas

nodes.name: Axioms of similarity and congruence
nodes.statement: $\emph{\textbf{ \cite[Definitions 5.6.1, 5.6.5]{Ha98}}}$ Let $\approx$ be a binary predicate symbol, the following are the axioms of similarity and congruence: \begin{itemize} \item[S1.] $(\forall x)x\approx x$ \item[S2.] $(\forall x)(\forall y)(x\approx y\rightarrow y\approx x$) \item[S3.] $(\forall x)(\forall y)(\forall z)(x\approx y \& y\approx z\rightarrow x\approx z)$ \end{itemize} \begin{itemize} \item[C1.] For each $n$-ary function symbol $F$, \end{itemize} {\footnotesize $(\forall x_1)\dotsb(\forall x_n)(\forall y_1)\dotsb(\forall y_n)(x_1\approx y_1\&\dotsb \& x_n\approx y_n\rightarrow F(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\approx F(y_1,\ldots,y_n))$ } \begin{itemize} \item[C2.] For each $n$-ary predicate symbol $P$, \end{itemize} {\footnotesize $(\forall x_1)\dotsb(\forall x_n)(\forall y_1)\dotsb(\forall y_n)(x_1\approx y_1\&\dotsb \& x_n\approx y_n\rightarrow (P(x_1, \ldots, x_n)\leftrightarrow P(y_1,\ldots, y_n)))$ }
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
nodes.label: def similarity

nodes.name: Relation $\sim$ on terms
nodes.statement: Let $\Phi$ be a set of formulas, we define a binary relation on the set of terms, denoted by $\sim$, in the following way: for every terms $t_1,t_2$, \begin{center} $t_1\sim t_2$ if and only if $\Phi\vdash t_1\approx t_2$. \end{center}
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
nodes.statement_short: $t_1\sim t_2$ iff $\Phi$ proves $t_1\approx t_2$.
nodes.label: relacio

nodes.name: $\sim$ is an equivalence relation
nodes.statement: By using \cite[Prop.1(5)]{EsGo01}, it is easy to check that for every set of formulas $\Phi$, $\sim$ is an equivalence relation.
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
conclusions: $\sim$ is an equivalence relation

nodes.name: $\sim$-class $\overline{t}$
nodes.statement: From now on we denote by $\overline{t}$ the $\sim$-class of the term $t$.
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 1 (congruence axioms)
nodes.statement: The next result, which states that $\sim$ is compatible with the symbols of the language, can be easily proven using the Axioms of Congruence of Definition \ref{def similarity}.
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
nodes.statement_short: Follows directly from the congruence axioms C1, C2.

nodes.name: Compatibility of $\sim$ with the language
nodes.statement: Let $\Phi$ be a set of formulas. The relation $\sim$ has the following property: if for every $1\leq i\leq n$, $t_i\sim t'_i$, then \begin{itemize} \item[(i)] For any $n$-ary function symbol $F$, $F(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\sim F(t'_1,\ldots,t'_n)$, \item[(ii)] For any $n$-ary predicate symbol $P$, \small{ $\Phi\vdash P(t_1,\ldots, t_n)$ \text{iff} $\Phi\vdash P(t'_1, \ldots, t'_n)$} \end{itemize}
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
assumptions: Let $\Phi$ be a set of formulas.
conclusions: For any $n$-ary function symbol $F$, $F(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\sim F(t'_1,\ldots,t'_n)$
For any $n$-ary predicate symbol $P$, \small{ $\Phi\vdash P(t_1,\ldots, t_n)$ \text{iff} $\Phi\vdash P(t'_1, \ldots, t'_n)$}
nodes.statement_short: $\sim$ is a congruence: preserved by function symbols and by provability of atomic predicates.
nodes.label: f

nodes.name: Term Structure
nodes.statement: Let $\Phi$ be a consistent set of formulas. We define the following structure $\langle\textbf{B},\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi}\rangle$, where $\textbf{B}$ is the two-valued Boolean algebra, $\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi}$ is the set of all equivalence classes of the relation $\sim$ and \begin{itemize} \item For any $n$-ary function symbol $F$, $$F_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi}}(\overline{t}_1,\ldots,\overline{t}_n)=\overline{F(t_1,\ldots,t_n)}$$ \item For any $n$-ary predicate symbol $P$, $$ P_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi}}(\overline{t}_1,\ldots,\overline{t}_n)=\begin{cases} 1, & \mbox{if } \Phi\vdash P(t_1,\ldots, t_n) \\ 0, & \mbox{otherwise } \end{cases} $$ \end{itemize} We call $\langle\textbf{B},\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi}\rangle$ the \emph{term structure associated to $\Phi$}.
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
nodes.statement_short: Two-valued structure on $\sim$-classes of terms: functions act syntactically, $P$ holds iff $\Phi$ proves it.
nodes.label: structure

nodes.name: Term structure is well-defined
nodes.statement: By using Lemma \ref{f}, it is easy to prove that the structure $\langle\emph{\textbf{B}},\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi}\rangle$ is well-defined, because the conditions are independent from the choice of the representatives.
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas

nodes.name: Term structure is classical
nodes.statement: Observe that, so defined, $\langle\emph{\textbf{B}},\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi}\rangle$ is a classical structure.
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
conclusions: $\langle\emph{\textbf{B}},\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi}\rangle$ is a classical structure

nodes.name: Crispness of $\approx$ in the term structure
nodes.statement: Let $\Phi$ be a consistent set of formulas. The interpretation of the $\approx$ symbol in the structure $\langle\textbf{B},\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi}\rangle$ is the crisp equality.
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
assumptions: Let $\Phi$ be a consistent set of formulas.
conclusions: The interpretation of the $\approx$ symbol in the structure $\langle\textbf{B},\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi}\rangle$ is the crisp equality.
nodes.label: crisp

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2
nodes.statement: Let $t_1,t_2$ be terms. We have $\overline{t}_1=\overline{t}_2$ iff $t_1\sim t_2$ iff $\Phi\vdash t_1\approx t_2$ iff $\overline{t_1}\approx_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi}} \overline{t_2}$ (this last step by Definition \ref{structure}).
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
nodes.statement_short: Chain of equivalences through $\sim$ and the definition of the term structure.

nodes.name: Canonical evaluation
nodes.statement: Given a consistent set of formulas $\Phi$, let $e^{\Phi}$ be the following $\emph{\textbf{T}}^{\Phi}$-evaluation: $e^{\Phi}(x)=\overline{x}$. We call $e^{\Phi}$ the \emph{canonical evaluation of} $\langle\textbf{B},\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi}\rangle$.
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
nodes.label: canonical

nodes.name: Terms and atomic formulas in the term structure
nodes.statement: Let $\Phi$ be a consistent set of formulas, the following holds: \begin{itemize} \item[(i)] For any term $t$, $|| t ||^{\textbf{B}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}=\overline{t}$. \item[(ii)] For any atomic formula $\varphi$, $|| \varphi||^{\textbf{B}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}=1$ if and only if $\Phi\vdash\varphi$. \item[(iii)] For any atomic formula $\varphi$, $|| \varphi||^{\textbf{B}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}=0$ if and only if $\Phi\not \vdash\varphi$. \end{itemize}
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
assumptions: Let $\Phi$ be a consistent set of formulas
conclusions: For any term $t$, $|| t ||^{\textbf{B}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}=\overline{t}$.
For any atomic formula $\varphi$, $|| \varphi||^{\textbf{B}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}=1$ if and only if $\Phi\vdash\varphi$.
For any atomic formula $\varphi$, $|| \varphi||^{\textbf{B}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}=0$ if and only if $\Phi\not \vdash\varphi$.
nodes.statement_short: Under the canonical evaluation, terms evaluate to their classes and an atomic formula is true iff $\Phi$ proves it.
nodes.label: terms and atomic formulas

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3
nodes.statement: (i) By induction on the complexity of $t$ and Definitions \ref{structure} and \ref{canonical}. \newline (ii) Let $P$ be an $n$-ary predicate symbol and $t_1,\ldots,t_n$ be terms, we have: \medskip$\begin{array}{rr} ||P(t_1,\ldots,t_n)||^{\emph{\textbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}=1 & \text{iff} \\[2ex] P_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi}}(|| t_1 ||^{\emph{\textbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}},\ldots,|| t_n ||^{\emph{\textbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}})=1 & \text{iff} \\[2ex] P_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi}}(\overline{t}_1,\ldots,\overline{t}_n)=1 & \text{iff} \\[2ex] \Phi\vdash P(t_1,\ldots, t_n) & \end{array}$ \medskip \noindent The second equivalence is by (i) of the present Lemma, and the third one by Definition \ref{structure}. (iii) holds because $\langle\emph{\textbf{B}},\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi}\rangle$ is a classical structure.
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
nodes.statement_short: (i) by induction on terms; (ii) by a chain of equivalences using (i) and the term-structure definition; (iii) by classicality.

nodes.name: Minimality of term structures w.r.t. atomic formulas
nodes.statement: Observe that, since terms are the smallest significance components of a first-order language, Lemma \ref{terms and atomic formulas} (ii) and (iii) can be read as saying that term structures are minimal with respect to atomic formulas. Intuitively speaking, the term structure picks up the positive atomic information associated to $\Phi$.
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas

nodes.name: Variables generate the term structure
nodes.statement: Let $\Phi$ be a consistent set of formulas. The set $\{\overline{x}\mid x\in Var\}$ generates the universe $T^{\Phi}$ of the term structure associated to $\Phi$.
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
assumptions: Let $\Phi$ be a consistent set of formulas.
conclusions: The set $\{\overline{x}\mid x\in Var\}$ generates the universe $T^{\Phi}$ of the term structure associated to $\Phi$.
nodes.label: generates

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4
nodes.statement: Let $\overline{t(x_1,\ldots,x_n)}\in T^{\Phi}$. By Lemma \ref{terms and atomic formulas}, $$\overline{t(x_1,\ldots,x_n)}=||t(x_1,\ldots,x_n) ||^{\emph{\textbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}$$ and by the semantics of predicate fuzzy logics (Definition \ref{evaluation}), \begin{center} $||t(x_1,\ldots,x_n) ||^{\emph{\textbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}=t_{T^{\Phi}}(||x_1||^{\emph{\textbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}},\ldots,||x_n ||^{\emph{\textbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}})=t_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi}}(\overline{x}_1,\ldots,\overline{x}_n)$. \end{center}
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
nodes.statement_short: Each class $\overline{t}$ is the value of $t$ under the canonical evaluation, hence a term function of the $\overline{x}_i$.

nodes.name: Free model
nodes.statement: A model of a theory is free if there is a unique homomorphism from this model to any other model of the theory.
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
differentia: there is a unique homomorphism from this model to any other model of the theory
also_stated_at: Free structures of a given class are minimal from an algebraic point of view, in the sense that there is a unique homomorphism from these structures to any other structure in the class.

nodes.name: Reduced structure
nodes.statement: Remember that \emph{reduced structures} are those whose Leibniz congruence is the identity.
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
differentia: whose Leibniz congruence is the identity

nodes.name: Reduced iff equality property (Dellunde Lemma 20)
nodes.statement: By \cite[Lemma 20]{De12}, a structure $\langle\emph{\textbf{A}},\mathrm{\mathbf{M}}\rangle$ is reduced iff it has the \emph{equality property} (EQP) (that is, for any $d,e\in M$, $d\approx_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}}} e$ iff $d=e$).
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
conclusions: a structure $\langle\emph{\textbf{A}},\mathrm{\mathbf{M}}\rangle$ is reduced iff it has the \emph{equality property} (EQP)

nodes.name: Term structure is free in reduced models
nodes.statement: Let $\Phi$ be a consistent set of formulas with $|| \Phi||^{\textbf{B}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}=1$. Then, $\langle\textbf{B},\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi}\rangle$ is a free structure in the class of the reduced models of $\Phi$, i.e., for every reduced structure $\langle\textbf{A},\mathrm{\mathbf{M}}\rangle$ and every evaluation $v$ such that $|| \Phi||^{\textbf{A}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v}=1$, there is a unique homomorphism $\langle f,g\rangle$ from $\langle\textbf{B},\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi}\rangle$ to $\langle\textbf{A},\mathrm{\mathbf{M}}\rangle$ such that for every $x \in Var$, $g(\overline{x})=v(x)$.
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
assumptions: Let $\Phi$ be a consistent set of formulas with $|| \Phi||^{\textbf{B}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}=1$.
conclusions: $\langle\textbf{B},\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi}\rangle$ is a free structure in the class of the reduced models of $\Phi$
nodes.statement_short: If the term structure of a consistent $\Phi$ satisfies $\Phi$, it is free (unique homomorphism extending any evaluation) among reduced models.
nodes.label: initial model

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement: Let $\langle\emph{\textbf{A}},\mathrm{\mathbf{M}}\rangle$ be a reduced structure and $v$ an $\textbf{M}$-evaluation such that $|| \Phi||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v}=1$. Now let $f:\emph{\textbf{B}}\rightarrow\emph{\textbf{A}}$ be the identity and define $g$ by: $g(\overline{t})=|| t ||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v}$ for every term $t$. We show that $\langle f,g\rangle$ is the desired homomorphism (for the definition of homomorphism see the Preliminaries section, Definition \ref{def:mapping structures}). First let us check that $g$ is well-defined. Given terms $t_1,t_2$ with $\overline{t}_1=\overline{t}_2$, that is, $t_1\sim t_2$, by Definition \ref{relacio}, $\Phi\vdash t_1\approx t_2$. Then, since $|| \Phi||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v}=1$, we have $|| t_1\approx t_2||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v}=1$. But $\langle\emph{\textbf{A}},\mathrm{\mathbf{M}}\rangle$ is reduced, which by \cite[Lemma 20]{De12} is equivalent to have the EQP; therefore $|| t_1 ||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v}=|| t_2||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v}$, that is, $g(\overline{t_1})=g(\overline{t_2})$. Now, let us see that $g$ is a homomorphism. Let $\overline{t}_1,\ldots,\overline{t}_n\in T^{\Phi}$ be terms and $F$ be an $n$-ary function symbol. By Definition \ref{structure}, we have that $$F_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi}}(\overline{t}_1,\ldots,\overline{t}_n)=\overline{F(t_1,\ldots,t_n)}$$ and then $g(F_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi}}(\overline{t}_1,\ldots,\overline{t}_n))=g(\overline{F(t_1,\ldots,t_n)})=|| F(t_1,\ldots,t_n) ||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v}= \newline =F_{\textbf{M}}(|| t_1||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v},\ldots ,|| t_n ||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v})= F_{\textbf{M}}(g(\overline{t}_1),\ldots,g(\overline{t}_n))$. \bigskip Let $P$ be an $n$-ary predicate symbol such that $P_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi}}(\overline{t}_1,\ldots,\overline{t}_n)=1$. By Definition \ref{structure}, $\Phi\vdash P(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$. Since $|| \Phi||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v}=1$, we have $$|| P(t_1,\ldots,t_n)||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v}=1$$ and then $P_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}}}(|| t_1||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v},\ldots ,|| t_n ||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v})=1$, that is, $P_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}}}(g(\overline{t}_1),\ldots,g(\overline{t}_n))=1$. \medskip Finally, since by Lemma \ref{generates} the set $\{\overline{x}\mid x\in Var\}$ generates the universe $T^{\Phi}$ of the term structure associated to $\Phi$, $\langle f,g\rangle$ is the unique homomorphism such that for every $x \in Var$, $g(\overline{x})=v(x)$.
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
nodes.statement_short: Define $g(\overline{t})$ as the value of $t$ in $\mathbf{M}$; check well-definedness via EQP, the homomorphism conditions, and uniqueness since variables generate.

nodes.name: Term structure free in all models under crisp identity
nodes.statement: Observe that in languages in which the similarity symbol is interpreted by the crisp identity, by using an analogous argument to the one in Theorem \ref{initial model}, we obtain that the term structure is free in all the models of the theory and not only in the class of reduced models.
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
assumptions: in languages in which the similarity symbol is interpreted by the crisp identity
conclusions: the term structure is free in all the models of the theory and not only in the class of reduced models

nodes.name: Rank of a formula
nodes.statement: We introduce first the notion of \emph{rank of a formula} $\varphi$. Our definition is a variant of the notion of \emph{syntactic degree of a formula} in \cite[Definition 5.6.7]{Ha98}). \begin{description} \item $rk(\varphi)=0$, if $\varphi$ is atomic; \item $rk(\neg\varphi)=rk((\exists x)\varphi)=rk((\forall x)\varphi)=rk(\varphi)+1$; \item $rk(\varphi\circ\psi)=rk(\varphi)+rk(\psi)$, for every binary propositional connective $\circ$. \end{description}
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
nodes.statement_short: Rank counts negations and quantifiers, adding over binary connectives; atomic formulas have rank 0.

nodes.name: Substitution preserves (w-)Horn clauses
nodes.statement: Let $\varphi$ be a (w-)Horn clause where $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ are pairwise distinct free variables. Then, for every terms $t_1,\ldots,t_m$, $$\varphi (t_1,\ldots,t_m/x_1,\ldots,x_m)$$ is a (w-)Horn clause.
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
assumptions: Let $\varphi$ be a (w-)Horn clause where $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ are pairwise distinct free variables.
conclusions: for every terms $t_1,\ldots,t_m$, $$\varphi (t_1,\ldots,t_m/x_1,\ldots,x_m)$$ is a (w-)Horn clause.
nodes.label: Horn substitucio

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5
nodes.statement: We prove it for the strong conjunction but the proof is analogous for the weak conjunction. By induction on $rk(\varphi)$. \bigskip \underline{Case $rk(\varphi)=0$}. If $\varphi$ is a basic Horn formula of the form $\psi_1\& \ldots \&\psi_n\rightarrow\psi$, it is clear that $\varphi (t_1,\ldots,t_m/x_1,\ldots,x_m)$ is still a basic Horn formula. In case that $\varphi=\phi_1\& \dotsb\&\phi_l$ is a conjunction of basic Horn formulas, note that $\varphi (t_1,\ldots,t_m/x_1,\ldots,x_m)$ has the same form as $\varphi$. \bigskip \underline{Case $rk(\varphi)=n+1$}. Assume inductively that for any Horn clause $\psi$ where $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ are pairwise distinct free variables in $\psi$ and whose rank is $n$, the formula $\psi (t_1,\ldots,t_m/x_1,\ldots,x_m)$ is a Horn clause. Let $\varphi$ be a Horn clause of rank $n+1$, then $\varphi$ is of the form $(\forall y)\psi$, where $\psi$ has rank $n$. Assume without loss of generality that and $y\not\in\{x_1,\ldots,x_m\}$, then$$[(\forall y)\psi](t_1,\ldots,t_m/x_1,\ldots,x_m)=(\forall y)[\psi(t_1,\ldots,t_m/x_1,\ldots,x_m)]$$ thus we can apply the inductive hypothesis to obtain the desired result.
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $rk(\varphi)$: rank 0 forms are preserved by substitution; a universal quantifier commutes with substitution.

nodes.name: Term structure satisfies provable Horn clauses
nodes.statement: Let $\Phi$ be a consistent set of formulas. For every (w-)Horn clause $\varphi$, if $\Phi\vdash\varphi$, then $|| \varphi||^{\textbf{B}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}=1$.
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
assumptions: Let $\Phi$ be a consistent set of formulas.
conclusions: $|| \varphi||^{\textbf{B}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}=1$
nodes.statement_short: Every (w-)Horn clause provable from a consistent $\Phi$ holds in the term structure under the canonical evaluation.
nodes.label: theorem Horn formulas

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement:
We prove it for the strong conjunction but the proof is analogous for the weak conjunction. By induction on $rk(\varphi)$.  igskip \underline{Case $rk(\varphi)=0$.} We can distinguish two subcases: \medskip 1) If $\varphi=\psi_1\&\dotsb\&\psi_nightarrow\psi$ is a basic Horn formula, we have to show that $||\psi_1\&\dotsb\&\psi_n||^{\emph{	extbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}\leq|| \psi||^{\emph{	extbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}$. If $|| \psi||^{\emph{	extbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}=1$, we are done. Otherwise, by Definition ef{structure}, $\Phi
ot \vdash \psi$. Consequently, since $\Phi\vdash \psi_1\&\dotsb\&\psi_nightarrow\psi$, $\Phi
ot \vdash \psi_1\&\dotsb\&\psi_n$ and thus for some $1 \leq i \leq n$, $\Phi
ot \vdash \psi_i$. By Lemma ef{terms and atomic formulas} (ii), we have $|| \psi_i||^{\emph{	extbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}=0$ and then $||\psi_1\&\dotsb\&\psi_n||^{\emph{	extbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}=0$. Therefore, we can conclude $||\psi_1\&\dotsb\&\psi_n||^{\emph{	extbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}\leq|| \psi||^{\emph{	extbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}$. Note that if $n=0$, $\varphi$ is an atomic formula and the property holds by Lemma ef{terms and atomic formulas} (ii). \smallskip 2) If $\varphi=\psi_1\&\dotsb\&\psi_n$ is a conjunction of basic Horn formulas and $\Phi\vdash\varphi$, then for every $1 \leq i \leq n$, $\Phi\vdash \psi_i$. Thus, by 1), for every $1 \leq i \leq n$, $||\psi_i||^{\emph{	extbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}=1$ and then $|| \varphi||^{\emph{	extbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}=1$.  igskip \underline{Case $rk(\varphi)=n+1$.} \medskip If $\varphi=( orall x)\phi(x)$ is a Horn clause, where $rk(\phi(x))=n$ and $\Phi\vdash\varphi$, by Axiom \emph{$ orall 1$} of $L orall^m$, for every term $t$, $\Phi\vdash\phi(t/x)$. Since by Lemma ef{Horn substitucio}, $\phi(t/x)$ is also a Horn clause and $rk(\phi(t/x))=n$, we can apply the inductive hypothesis and hence for every term $t$, $||\phi(t/x)||^{\emph{	extbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}=1$, that is, by Lemma ef{terms and atomic formulas} (i), for every element $\overline{t}$ of the domain, $||\phi(x)||^{\emph{	extbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}(xightarrow\overline{t})}=1$. Therefore, we can conclude that $||( orall x)\phi(x)||^{\emph{	extbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}=1$.
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $rk(\varphi)$. Rank 0 handled via Lemma 3 for basic Horn formulas and conjunctions; the quantifier step uses axiom $\forall 1$ and Lemma 5.

nodes.statement_short: In Goedel logic, $\Phi=\{\neg(Pc\to 0)\}$ and $\varphi=Pc\to 0$: true in the term structure but not provable.

nodes.name: Converse of Theorem 2 is false
nodes.statement: Observe that the inverse direction of Theorem \ref{theorem Horn formulas} is not true.
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
conclusions: the inverse direction of Theorem \ref{theorem Horn formulas} is not true

nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
nodes.statement_short: Counterexample: a [0,1] Goedel structure with $Pc=0.8$ shows non-provability, while Lemma 3 makes $\varphi$ true in the term structure.

nodes.name: Ground-term substructure is a model of Horn consequences
nodes.statement: Remark that, as a corollary of Theorem \ref{theorem Horn formulas}, we have that the substructure of $\langle\emph{\textbf{B}},\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi}\rangle$ generated by the set of ground terms is also a model for all universal Horn sentences that are consequences of the theory.
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
conclusions: the substructure of $\langle\emph{\textbf{B}},\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi}\rangle$ generated by the set of ground terms is also a model for all universal Horn sentences that are consequences of the theory

nodes.name: Corollary 1 from Theorem 2
nodes.statement: Another important corollary of Theorem \ref{theorem Horn formulas} is the following:
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
nodes.statement_short: Immediate consequence of Theorem 2.

nodes.name: Consistent Horn sentences have classical models
nodes.statement: Every consistent set of (w-)Horn clauses without free variables has a classical model.
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
assumptions: consistent set of (w-)Horn clauses without free variables
conclusions: has a classical model
nodes.label: classic

nodes.name: Non-Horn consistent sentence without classical model
nodes.statement: Observe that Corollary \ref{classic} is not true in general. The consistent sentence $\neg (\overline{1} \to Pa) \& \neg (Pa \to \overline{0})$ has no classical model.
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
nodes.statement_short: $\neg(1\to Pa)\&\neg(Pa\to 0)$ is consistent but has no classical model.

nodes.name: Equality-free formula
nodes.statement: They are a prominent form of term structures, specially helpful when dealing with sets of equality-free formulas (that is, formulas in which the symbol $\approx$ does not occur), the reason is that, as it is shown below in Lemma \ref{equality}, no non-trivial equations are derivable from a set of equality-free formulas.
nodes.section: 5 Herbrand Structures
differentia: formulas in which the symbol $\approx$ does not occur

nodes.name: Crisp identity and an individual constant
nodes.statement: Throughout this section we assume that the symbol $\approx$ is interpreted always as the crisp identity and that there is at least an individual constant in the language.
nodes.section: 5 Herbrand Structures

nodes.name: No non-trivial equations from equality-free theories
nodes.statement: Let $\Phi$ be a consistent set of equality-free formulas, then for every terms $t_1,t_2$, $$ \text{If }\Phi\vdash t_1\approx t_2, \text{ then }t_1=t_2.$$
nodes.section: 5 Herbrand Structures
assumptions: Let $\Phi$ be a consistent set of equality-free formulas
conclusions: for every terms $t_1,t_2$, $$ \text{If }\Phi\vdash t_1\approx t_2, \text{ then }t_1=t_2.$$
nodes.label: equality

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6
nodes.statement: Assume that $\Phi$ is a consistent set of equality-free formulas and $\Phi\vdash t_1\approx t_2$ for terms $t_1,t_2$ of the language. Since CL$\forall$ is an extension of MTL$\forall^m$, $\Phi\vdash t_1\approx t_2$ in CL$\forall$. Then, by the analogous classical result \cite[Ch. 11, Th. 3.1]{EbiFlu94}, we have $t_1=t_2$.
nodes.section: 5 Herbrand Structures
nodes.statement_short: Transfer the derivation to classical logic CL$\forall$ and apply the classical result of Ebbinghaus-Flum-Thomas.

nodes.name: Herbrand Structure
nodes.statement: The \emph{Herbrand universe of a predicate language} is the set of all ground terms of the language. A \emph{Herbrand structure} is a structure $\langle\textbf{A},\emph{\textbf{H}}\rangle$, where $\emph{\textbf{H}}$ is the Herbrand universe, and: \begin{itemize} \item[] For any individual constant symbol $c$, $c_{\emph{\textbf{H}}}=c$. \item[] For any $n$-ary function symbol $F$ and any $t_1,\ldots,t_n\in H$, \begin{center} \smallskip $F_{\emph{\textbf{H}}}(t_1,\ldots,t_n)=F(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$ \end{center} \end{itemize}
nodes.section: 5 Herbrand Structures
nodes.statement_short: Herbrand universe = ground terms; a Herbrand structure has it as domain with constants and functions interpreted syntactically.
nodes.label: Herbrand structure

nodes.name: Canonical models are Herbrand structures
nodes.statement: The canonical models $\langle\emph{\textbf{Lind}}_{T},\mathbf{CM}(T)\rangle$ introduced in {\cite[Def.9]{CiHa06} are examples of Herbrand structures. In these structures $\emph{\textbf{Lind}}_{T}$ is the Lindenbaum algebra of a theory $T$ and the domain of $\mathbf{CM}(T)$ is the set of individual constants (the language in \cite{CiHa06} do not contain function symbols).
nodes.section: 5 Herbrand Structures

nodes.name: H-structure and H-model
nodes.statement: Let $\overline{H}$ be the set of all \newline equality-free sentences of the form $P(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$, where $t_1,\ldots,t_n$ are ground terms, $n\geq 1$ and $P$ is an $n$-ary predicate symbol. For every subset $H$ of $\overline{H}$, we define the Herbrand structure $\langle\textbf{B},\mathbf{N}^{\emph{H}}\rangle$, where $\textbf{B}$ is the two-valued Boolean algebra, the domain $\mathbf{N}^{\emph{H}}$ is the set of all ground terms of the language, the interpretation of the function symbols is as in every Herbrand structure and the interpretation of the predicate symbols is as follows: for every $n\geq 1$ and every $n$-ary predicate symbol $P$, $$ P_{\mathrm{\mathbf{N}}^{\emph{H}}}(t_1,\ldots,t_n)=\begin{cases} 1, & \mbox{if } P(t_1,\ldots,t_n) \in H \\ 0, & \mbox{otherwise. } \end{cases} $$ We call this type of Herbrand structures \emph{H-structures}. If $\Phi$ is a set of sentences, we say that an \emph{H}-structure is an \emph{H-model} of $\Phi$ if it is a model of $\Phi$.
nodes.section: 5 Herbrand Structures
nodes.statement_short: Two-valued Herbrand structure whose true atomic sentences are exactly a chosen set $H$; an H-model is one that models $\Phi$.
nodes.label: Herbrand boolean

nodes.name: Horn clauses transfer to the associated H-structure
nodes.statement: Let $\langle\textbf{A},\mathbf{M}\rangle$ be a structure and H be the set of all atomic equality-free sentences $\sigma$ such that $||\sigma||^{\textbf{A}}_{\emph{\textbf{M}}}=1$. Then, for every equality-free sentence $\varphi$ which is a (w-)Horn clause, if $||\varphi||^{\textbf{A}}_{\emph{\textbf{M}}}=1$, then $||\varphi||^{\textbf{B}}_{\emph{\textbf{N}}^{\emph{H}}}=1$, where $\langle\textbf{B},\emph{\textbf{N}}^{\emph{H}}\rangle$ is an \emph{H}-structure as in Definition \ref{Herbrand boolean}.
nodes.section: 5 Herbrand Structures
assumptions: Let $\langle\textbf{A},\mathbf{M}\rangle$ be a structure and H be the set of all atomic equality-free sentences $\sigma$ such that $||\sigma||^{\textbf{A}}_{\emph{\textbf{M}}}=1$.
equality-free sentence $\varphi$ which is a (w-)Horn clause
conclusions: $||\varphi||^{\textbf{B}}_{\emph{\textbf{N}}^{\emph{H}}}=1$
nodes.statement_short: Equality-free Horn sentences true in a structure remain true in the H-structure of its true atomic sentences.
nodes.label: proposition

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 1
nodes.section: 5 Herbrand Structures
nodes.statement_short: Induction on rank: basic Horn formulas and conjunctions at rank 0, universal quantifier via axiom $\forall 1$, Lemma 5 and the Herbrand domain.

nodes.name: H-structure can satisfy more Horn sentences
nodes.statement: Notice that Proposition \ref{proposition} does not assert that given a structure $\langle\emph{\textbf{A}},\textbf{M}\rangle$, $\langle\emph{\textbf{A}},\textbf{M}\rangle$ and $\langle\emph{\textbf{B}},\textbf{N}^{\text{H}}\rangle$ satisfy exactly the same equality-free sentences which are Horn clauses. Actually, this is not true. Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a predicate language with three monadic predicate symbols $P_1,P_2,P_3$ and one individual constant $c$. Suppose that $\emph{\textbf{A}}$ is the \L ukasiewicz algebra $[0,1]_{\text{\L}}$ and let $\langle\emph{\textbf{A}},\textbf{M}\rangle$ be a structure over $\mathcal{P}$ such that $||P_1(c)||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\textbf{M}}=1$, $||P_2(c)||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\textbf{M}}=0.9$ and $||P_3(c)||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\textbf{M}}=0.5$. Let $\varphi$ be $P_1(c)\& P_2(c)\rightarrow P_3(c)$, $\varphi$ is an equality-free sentence which is a Horn clause with $||P_1(c)\& P_2(c)\rightarrow P_3(c)||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\textbf{M}}=0.6$, but if we consider its associated H-structure, $\langle\emph{\textbf{B}},\textbf{N}^{\text{H}}\rangle$, we have H$=\{P_1(c)\}$ and thus $||P_1(c)\& P_2(c)\rightarrow P_3(c)||^{\emph{\textbf{B}}}_{\textbf{N}^{\text{H}}}=1$.
nodes.section: 5 Herbrand Structures
nodes.statement_short: In Lukasiewicz logic a Horn sentence with value 0.6 becomes true in the associated H-structure, so the converse of Proposition 1 fails.

nodes.name: Equality-free Horn sentence has a model iff an H-model
nodes.statement: An equality-free sentence which is a (w-)Horn clause has a model if and only if it has an \emph{H}-model.
nodes.section: 5 Herbrand Structures
assumptions: An equality-free sentence which is a (w-)Horn clause
conclusions: has a model if and only if it has an \emph{H}-model
nodes.label: corollary H-model

nodes.name: Consistent equality-free Horn sentences have classical Herbrand models
nodes.statement: We can conclude here, in the same sense as in Corollary \ref{classic}, that every consistent equality-free sentence which is a (w-)Horn clause has a classical Herbrand model.
nodes.section: 5 Herbrand Structures
assumptions: every consistent equality-free sentence which is a (w-)Horn clause
conclusions: has a classical Herbrand model

nodes.name: Part (i)
nodes.statement: (i) By induction on the complexity of $t$ and Definitions \ref{structure} and \ref{canonical}. \newline
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
nodes.statement_short: Induction on the complexity of $t$.

nodes.name: Part (ii)
nodes.statement: (ii) Let $P$ be an $n$-ary predicate symbol and $t_1,\ldots,t_n$ be terms, we have: \medskip$\begin{array}{rr} ||P(t_1,\ldots,t_n)||^{\emph{\textbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}=1 & \text{iff} \\[2ex] P_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi}}(|| t_1 ||^{\emph{\textbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}},\ldots,|| t_n ||^{\emph{\textbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}})=1 & \text{iff} \\[2ex] P_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi}}(\overline{t}_1,\ldots,\overline{t}_n)=1 & \text{iff} \\[2ex] \Phi\vdash P(t_1,\ldots, t_n) & \end{array}$ \medskip \noindent The second equivalence is by (i) of the present Lemma, and the third one by Definition \ref{structure}.
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
nodes.statement_short: Chain of equivalences for atomic formulas via (i) and the term-structure definition.

nodes.name: Part (iii)
nodes.statement: (iii) holds because $\langle\emph{\textbf{B}},\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi}\rangle$ is a classical structure.
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
nodes.statement_short: Follows from the term structure being classical.

nodes.name: Construct the homomorphism
nodes.statement: Let $\langle\emph{\textbf{A}},\mathrm{\mathbf{M}}\rangle$ be a reduced structure and $v$ an $\textbf{M}$-evaluation such that $|| \Phi||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v}=1$. Now let $f:\emph{\textbf{B}}\rightarrow\emph{\textbf{A}}$ be the identity and define $g$ by: $g(\overline{t})=|| t ||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v}$ for every term $t$. We show that $\langle f,g\rangle$ is the desired homomorphism (for the definition of homomorphism see the Preliminaries section, Definition \ref{def:mapping structures}).
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
nodes.statement_short: Fix a reduced model and evaluation; let $f$ be the identity and $g(\overline{t})$ the value of $t$.

nodes.name: $g$ is well-defined
nodes.statement: First let us check that $g$ is well-defined. Given terms $t_1,t_2$ with $\overline{t}_1=\overline{t}_2$, that is, $t_1\sim t_2$, by Definition \ref{relacio}, $\Phi\vdash t_1\approx t_2$. Then, since $|| \Phi||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v}=1$, we have $|| t_1\approx t_2||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v}=1$. But $\langle\emph{\textbf{A}},\mathrm{\mathbf{M}}\rangle$ is reduced, which by \cite[Lemma 20]{De12} is equivalent to have the EQP; therefore $|| t_1 ||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v}=|| t_2||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v}$, that is, $g(\overline{t_1})=g(\overline{t_2})$.
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
nodes.statement_short: Show $g$ is well defined using EQP of reduced structures.

nodes.name: Equal classes are provably similar
nodes.statement: Given terms $t_1,t_2$ with $\overline{t}_1=\overline{t}_2$, that is, $t_1\sim t_2$, by Definition \ref{relacio}, $\Phi\vdash t_1\approx t_2$. Then, since $|| \Phi||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v}=1$, we have $|| t_1\approx t_2||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v}=1$.
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
nodes.statement_short: Equal classes give $\Phi\vdash t_1\approx t_2$, true in the model.

nodes.name: Use EQP
nodes.statement: But $\langle\emph{\textbf{A}},\mathrm{\mathbf{M}}\rangle$ is reduced, which by \cite[Lemma 20]{De12} is equivalent to have the EQP; therefore $|| t_1 ||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v}=|| t_2||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v}$, that is, $g(\overline{t_1})=g(\overline{t_2})$.
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
nodes.statement_short: Reducedness (EQP) turns similarity into equality of values.

nodes.name: $g$ preserves functions
nodes.statement: Now, let us see that $g$ is a homomorphism. Let $\overline{t}_1,\ldots,\overline{t}_n\in T^{\Phi}$ be terms and $F$ be an $n$-ary function symbol. By Definition \ref{structure}, we have that $$F_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi}}(\overline{t}_1,\ldots,\overline{t}_n)=\overline{F(t_1,\ldots,t_n)}$$ and then $g(F_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi}}(\overline{t}_1,\ldots,\overline{t}_n))=g(\overline{F(t_1,\ldots,t_n)})=|| F(t_1,\ldots,t_n) ||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v}= \newline =F_{\textbf{M}}(|| t_1||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v},\ldots ,|| t_n ||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v})= F_{\textbf{M}}(g(\overline{t}_1),\ldots,g(\overline{t}_n))$. \bigskip
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
nodes.statement_short: Check $g$ commutes with function symbols.

nodes.name: $g$ preserves true predicates
nodes.statement: Let $P$ be an $n$-ary predicate symbol such that $P_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi}}(\overline{t}_1,\ldots,\overline{t}_n)=1$. By Definition \ref{structure}, $\Phi\vdash P(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$. Since $|| \Phi||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v}=1$, we have $$|| P(t_1,\ldots,t_n)||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v}=1$$ and then $P_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}}}(|| t_1||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v},\ldots ,|| t_n ||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}},v})=1$, that is, $P_{\mathrm{\mathbf{M}}}(g(\overline{t}_1),\ldots,g(\overline{t}_n))=1$. \medskip
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
nodes.statement_short: Atomic facts true in the term structure are provable, hence true in $\mathbf{M}$.

nodes.name: Uniqueness
nodes.statement: Finally, since by Lemma \ref{generates} the set $\{\overline{x}\mid x\in Var\}$ generates the universe $T^{\Phi}$ of the term structure associated to $\Phi$, $\langle f,g\rangle$ is the unique homomorphism such that for every $x \in Var$, $g(\overline{x})=v(x)$.
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
nodes.statement_short: Uniqueness since the variable classes generate the universe (Lemma 4).

nodes.name: Setup: induction on rank
nodes.statement: We prove it for the strong conjunction but the proof is analogous for the weak conjunction. By induction on $rk(\varphi)$. \bigskip
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
nodes.statement_short: Strong conjunction case; induction on $rk(\varphi)$.

nodes.name: Case rank 0
nodes.statement: \underline{Case $rk(\varphi)=0$}. If $\varphi$ is a basic Horn formula of the form $\psi_1\& \ldots \&\psi_n\rightarrow\psi$, it is clear that $\varphi (t_1,\ldots,t_m/x_1,\ldots,x_m)$ is still a basic Horn formula. In case that $\varphi=\phi_1\& \dotsb\&\phi_l$ is a conjunction of basic Horn formulas, note that $\varphi (t_1,\ldots,t_m/x_1,\ldots,x_m)$ has the same form as $\varphi$. \bigskip
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
nodes.statement_short: Base case: basic Horn formulas and their conjunctions.

nodes.name: Case rank n+1
nodes.statement: \underline{Case $rk(\varphi)=n+1$}. Assume inductively that for any Horn clause $\psi$ where $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ are pairwise distinct free variables in $\psi$ and whose rank is $n$, the formula $\psi (t_1,\ldots,t_m/x_1,\ldots,x_m)$ is a Horn clause. Let $\varphi$ be a Horn clause of rank $n+1$, then $\varphi$ is of the form $(\forall y)\psi$, where $\psi$ has rank $n$. Assume without loss of generality that and $y\not\in\{x_1,\ldots,x_m\}$, then$$[(\forall y)\psi](t_1,\ldots,t_m/x_1,\ldots,x_m)=(\forall y)[\psi(t_1,\ldots,t_m/x_1,\ldots,x_m)]$$ thus we can apply the inductive hypothesis to obtain the desired result.
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
nodes.statement_short: Inductive step for a universally quantified Horn clause.

nodes.name: Setup: induction on rank
nodes.statement: We prove it for the strong conjunction but the proof is analogous for the weak conjunction. By induction on $rk(\varphi)$. \bigskip
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
nodes.statement_short: Strong conjunction case; induction on $rk(\varphi)$.

nodes.name: Case rank 0
nodes.statement:
\underline{Case $rk(\varphi)=0$.} We can distinguish two subcases: \medskip 1) If $\varphi=\psi_1\&\dotsb\&\psi_nightarrow\psi$ is a basic Horn formula, we have to show that $||\psi_1\&\dotsb\&\psi_n||^{\emph{	extbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}\leq|| \psi||^{\emph{	extbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}$. If $|| \psi||^{\emph{	extbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}=1$, we are done. Otherwise, by Definition ef{structure}, $\Phi
ot \vdash \psi$. Consequently, since $\Phi\vdash \psi_1\&\dotsb\&\psi_nightarrow\psi$, $\Phi
ot \vdash \psi_1\&\dotsb\&\psi_n$ and thus for some $1 \leq i \leq n$, $\Phi
ot \vdash \psi_i$. By Lemma ef{terms and atomic formulas} (ii), we have $|| \psi_i||^{\emph{	extbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}=0$ and then $||\psi_1\&\dotsb\&\psi_n||^{\emph{	extbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}=0$. Therefore, we can conclude $||\psi_1\&\dotsb\&\psi_n||^{\emph{	extbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}\leq|| \psi||^{\emph{	extbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}$. Note that if $n=0$, $\varphi$ is an atomic formula and the property holds by Lemma ef{terms and atomic formulas} (ii). \smallskip 2) If $\varphi=\psi_1\&\dotsb\&\psi_n$ is a conjunction of basic Horn formulas and $\Phi\vdash\varphi$, then for every $1 \leq i \leq n$, $\Phi\vdash \psi_i$. Thus, by 1), for every $1 \leq i \leq n$, $||\psi_i||^{\emph{	extbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}=1$ and then $|| \varphi||^{\emph{	extbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}=1$.  igskip
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
nodes.statement_short: Base case: basic Horn formulas and their conjunctions.

nodes.name: Subcase 1: basic Horn formula
nodes.statement:
1) If $\varphi=\psi_1\&\dotsb\&\psi_nightarrow\psi$ is a basic Horn formula, we have to show that $||\psi_1\&\dotsb\&\psi_n||^{\emph{	extbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}\leq|| \psi||^{\emph{	extbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}$. If $|| \psi||^{\emph{	extbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}=1$, we are done. Otherwise, by Definition ef{structure}, $\Phi
ot \vdash \psi$. Consequently, since $\Phi\vdash \psi_1\&\dotsb\&\psi_nightarrow\psi$, $\Phi
ot \vdash \psi_1\&\dotsb\&\psi_n$ and thus for some $1 \leq i \leq n$, $\Phi
ot \vdash \psi_i$. By Lemma ef{terms and atomic formulas} (ii), we have $|| \psi_i||^{\emph{	extbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}=0$ and then $||\psi_1\&\dotsb\&\psi_n||^{\emph{	extbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}=0$. Therefore, we can conclude $||\psi_1\&\dotsb\&\psi_n||^{\emph{	extbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}\leq|| \psi||^{\emph{	extbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}$. Note that if $n=0$, $\varphi$ is an atomic formula and the property holds by Lemma ef{terms and atomic formulas} (ii). \smallskip
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
nodes.statement_short: If the head is false in the term structure, some premise is unprovable, so the premise conjunction is 0 (Lemma 3).

nodes.name: Subcase 2: conjunction
nodes.statement: 2) If $\varphi=\psi_1\&\dotsb\&\psi_n$ is a conjunction of basic Horn formulas and $\Phi\vdash\varphi$, then for every $1 \leq i \leq n$, $\Phi\vdash \psi_i$. Thus, by 1), for every $1 \leq i \leq n$, $||\psi_i||^{\emph{\textbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}=1$ and then $|| \varphi||^{\emph{\textbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}=1$. \bigskip
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
nodes.statement_short: A provable conjunction has provable conjuncts, each true by subcase 1.

nodes.name: Case rank n+1
nodes.statement: \underline{Case $rk(\varphi)=n+1$.} \medskip If $\varphi=(\forall x)\phi(x)$ is a Horn clause, where $rk(\phi(x))=n$ and $\Phi\vdash\varphi$, by Axiom \emph{$\forall 1$} of $L\forall^m$, for every term $t$, $\Phi\vdash\phi(t/x)$. Since by Lemma \ref{Horn substitucio}, $\phi(t/x)$ is also a Horn clause and $rk(\phi(t/x))=n$, we can apply the inductive hypothesis and hence for every term $t$, $||\phi(t/x)||^{\emph{\textbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}=1$, that is, by Lemma \ref{terms and atomic formulas} (i), for every element $\overline{t}$ of the domain, $||\phi(x)||^{\emph{\textbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}(x\rightarrow\overline{t})}=1$. Therefore, we can conclude that $||(\forall x)\phi(x)||^{\emph{\textbf{B}}}_{\mathrm{\mathbf{T}}^{\Phi},e^{\Phi}}=1$.
nodes.section: 4 Term structures associated to a set of formulas
nodes.statement_short: Inductive step for a universally quantified Horn clause.

nodes.name: Setup: induction on rank
nodes.statement: We prove it for the strong conjunction but the proof is analogous for the weak conjunction. Assume that $\varphi$ is an equality-free sentence which is a Horn clause and $||\varphi||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\textbf{M}}=1$. We proceed by induction on the rank of $\varphi$ \bigskip
nodes.section: 5 Herbrand Structures
nodes.statement_short: Strong conjunction case; induction on $rk(\varphi)$.

nodes.name: Case rank 0
nodes.section: 5 Herbrand Structures
nodes.statement_short: Base case: basic Horn formulas and their conjunctions.

nodes.name: Subcase 1: basic Horn formula
nodes.section: 5 Herbrand Structures
nodes.statement_short: If the head is false in the H-structure it is not in H, so some premise fails in $\mathbf{M}$ and is 0 in the H-structure.

nodes.name: Subcase 2: conjunction
nodes.statement: 2) If $\varphi=\psi_1\&\dotsb\&\psi_n$ is a strong conjunction of basic Horn formulas, then by 1) we have that $||\psi_i||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\textbf{M}}=1$ implies $||\psi_i||^{\emph{\textbf{B}}}_{\textbf{N}^{\text{H}}}=1$, for each $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Thus, if $||\varphi||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\textbf{M}}=1$, then $||\varphi||^{\emph{\textbf{B}}}_{\textbf{N}^{\text{H}}}=1$. \bigskip
nodes.section: 5 Herbrand Structures
nodes.statement_short: Each conjunct transfers by subcase 1.

nodes.name: Case rank n+1
nodes.statement: \underline{Case $rk(\varphi)=n+1$.} \bigskip Let $\varphi=(\forall x)\phi(x)$ be a Horn clause with $rk(\phi(x))=n$. Since $||\varphi||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\textbf{M}}=1$, by Axiom \emph{$\forall 1$} of $L\forall^m$, for every ground term $t$, $||\phi(t/x)||^{\emph{\textbf{A}}}_{\textbf{M}}=1$. By Lemma \ref{Horn substitucio}, $\phi(t/x)$ is also a Horn clause, and since $rk(\phi(t/x))=n$, we can apply the inductive hypothesis and hence for every ground term $t$, $||\phi(t/x)|^{\emph{\textbf{B}}}_{\textbf{N}^{\text{H}}}=1$. Finally, since $\langle\emph{\textbf{B}},\mathbf{N}^{\text{H}}\rangle$ is a Herbrand structure, we have that for every element $t$ of its domain $||\phi(t/x)||^{\emph{\textbf{B}}}_{\textbf{N}^{\text{H}}}=1$, and consequently $||(\forall x)\phi(x)||^{\emph{\textbf{B}}}_{\textbf{N}^{\text{H}}}=1$.
nodes.section: 5 Herbrand Structures
nodes.statement_short: Inductive step for a universally quantified Horn clause.

nodes.name: Assume derivation
nodes.statement: Assume that $\Phi$ is a consistent set of equality-free formulas and $\Phi\vdash t_1\approx t_2$ for terms $t_1,t_2$ of the language.
nodes.section: 5 Herbrand Structures
nodes.statement_short: Assume $\Phi$ equality-free and $\Phi\vdash t_1\approx t_2$.

nodes.name: Transfer to classical logic
nodes.statement: Since CL$\forall$ is an extension of MTL$\forall^m$, $\Phi\vdash t_1\approx t_2$ in CL$\forall$.
nodes.section: 5 Herbrand Structures
nodes.statement_short: Derivation holds in the classical extension CL$\forall$.

nodes.name: Apply classical result
nodes.statement: Then, by the analogous classical result \cite[Ch. 11, Th. 3.1]{EbiFlu94}, we have $t_1=t_2$.
nodes.section: 5 Herbrand Structures
nodes.statement_short: Classical result gives syntactic identity.
